simple.meaning: עָקַב (ʻâqab) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to seize by the heel ; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Genesis, Job, Jeremiah, Hosea, beginning at Genesis 27:36. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.

definitions.short: to seize by the heel ; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel)
definitions.usage: take by the heel, stay, supplant, × utterly.
definitions.full: H6117. aqab עָקַב verb follow at the heel , figurative assail insidiously, circumvent, overreach (denominative from עָקֵב ; compare Arabic follow (at the heel), succeed , III. bring consequence on , i.e. punish , Qor 22:59; IV. make to follow , i.e. reward or punish , end, final lot 6:11 reward 6:136 hold back (rare), follow , Pa`el investigate, search out: Ethiopic is keep, guard ); — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular Hosea 12:4 אֶתאָֿחִיו עָקַב בַּבֶּטֶן he attacked his brother at the heel (compare Gen 25:26 below עָקֵב ); Imperfect 3masculine singular 27:36 פַעֲמַיִם זֶה וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמוֺ קָרָא הֲכִי and he hath overreached me now twice; + Infinitive abs Jer 9:3 יַעֲקֹב עָקוֺב בָּלאָֿח surely overreacheth (|| יַהֲלֹח רָכִיל ). [ ᵐ5 πτερνίζω , to attack with the heel; but this dubious In 'supplant,' also, the figurative is a different one.] Pi`el Job 37:4 יְעַקְּבֵם וְלֹא dubious; poss attack at the heel (compare זִנֵּב ), hence figurative hold back ; more probably read יְעַכְּבֵם וְלֹא holdeth them not back (that is בְּרָקָיו his lightnings), when his voice is heard from עִכֵּב to hold back (common in Late Hebrew; עַכֵּב ᵑ7 ).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; properly, to swell out or up; used only as denominative from 6119 ,

occurrences.englishText: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”
Indeed, he struggled with the angel, and prevailed;
